raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year the way I always do.

---

I've been working this ground for thirty years. My father before me. Ten mu and a bit — not much, but enough if the weather holds and I don't waste money on things I don't need.

The six mu of flat ground near the road I put in wheat and then maize right after, same as everybody in our village. The other piece, close to five mu over by the ditch, has always been cotton. My father grew cotton there. The soil's a little sandy, grain doesn't do as well on it.

**Wheat first.** I plant around Cold Dew, middle of October, when the ground gets cool. Seeds I buy at the shop in town, whatever they're selling — I saved a little from last year's good patch but not enough for the whole six mu. Before I plant I spread one bag of the green-label compound per mu. Everybody uses that one. Then in spring when the wheat greens up, I put down about half a bag of urea per mu and water it in. I water three times if I can — before winter, when it greens up, and when the heads come. Pump costs money, but no water, no yield. Last year wheat gave me around 400 a mu. That's fine.

**Maize right after wheat.** The combine comes through in early June, then I've got maybe a week. My wife's brother has a no-till planter, I borrow it. Hybrid seed, whatever the shop says is good this year — I don't know one name from another, they know better. The planter puts fertilizer in with the seed. Then at the big-trumpet stage, late July, I put more urea on — about half a bag per mu. If it doesn't rain in July I water once. Usually gets me around 450 a mu.

**Cotton on the other piece.** I plant late April once the ground is warm. Cotton is a lot of work — the bugs come, I spray four or five times in summer for bollworm. I put compound before planting and urea when it flowers. My wife and I pick in the fall, three or four rounds. Her younger sister comes to help when we're busy, I pay her a bit. My older boy works in the city, doesn't come back. My younger one helps on weekends when school lets him. Last year cotton was a bit over 200 of lint. The price is better than grain but you earn it.

I don't plan to change much. My neighbor tried that expensive new wheat seed two years ago — same yield in the end. Save the money, keep some cash for when the pump breaks.
